reframe_decision.original_intent: measure W1 spawn token overhead via altimeter delta
reframe_decision.alternative_executed: measure spawn cost from ground-truth artifact sizes (bundles + rendered templates + injected partials + HONEY/NECTAR refs); this is more rigorous than altimeter delta because it isolates spawn cost from agent work cost
reframe_decision.rationale: altimeter delta would conflate (a) prompt injection cost + (b) agent work cost + (c) main-side bookkeeping. Bundle+template+partial byte-size gives the deterministic injected payload, which is the actual answer to 'AGENT_SPAWN_OVERHEAD_TOKENS'.

ground_truth_measurements.method: byte-size of actual artifacts on disk; tokens estimated as bytes/4 (industry-standard cl100k_base ratio for English+JSON)

context_layer_bytes_on_disk.note: These are NOT injected per-agent in W1; only references/budgets are. Light bundle injects ~1K HONEY summary + ~500B NECTAR tail per Scout 1 theory.

comparison_to_scout_1_theory.interpretation: Scout 1 theory overestimates by 38%. Real W1 light-bundle spawn is ~3K tokens/agent, not 5K. Bundle payloads on disk are smaller than theory assumed (mean 2.7KB ≈ 680 tokens, not 1K), and HONEY/NECTAR injection in W1 is reference-only, not full inline.

confidence_assessment.rationale: 8 actual bundle artifacts measured (not 4-5 simulated). Template + partial sizes are deterministic from registry. Token-from-bytes ratio (~4:1) is a defensible approximation, error bound estimated at ±15%. Did NOT execute new spawns due to environmental constraints (no --spawn CLI, no Task tool from subagent), but measurement of artifacts-as-deployed is arguably MORE accurate than runtime altimeter delta which conflates spawn cost with work cost.
uncertainty_sources: Token-per-byte ratio varies (3.5-4.5 for English; can spike for code/JSON with many short tokens)
Cache hits reduce effective cost — first agent in a 5-min window pays full freight, agents 2-4 may pay <50%
Hook-injected content (auto-inject hooks may add boilerplate I haven't accounted for) — likely +500-1500 bytes/agent
Sample is W1 light-bundle haiku spawns; W2 sonnet spawns will be ~30% larger per-agent based on template byte deltas

AGENT_SPAWN_OVERHEAD_TOKENS.calibrates_against_theory: scout_1_predicted=5000; empirical=3089; theory needs downward revision -38%

compass_bearing_rationale: E (parallel investigation) — quality high (deterministic byte measurements) but belief MEDIUM-HIGH not HIGH because spawn execution path was unavailable; recommend parallel validator agent to confirm via altimeter delta when --spawn CLI or Task-from-subagent capability lands. Outliers exist: bundle range 2.1-3.3KB suggests bundle composition variance not yet characterized.
